text.p: Grain and oilseed exports reported by USDA and private export sources.
CORN SALE - Taiwan's CK group on Wednesday bought two 54,000-tonne shipments of U.S. No.2 corn from Agrex and Kanematsu, traders said.

SOYBEAN SALE - Glencore Brazil has sold 45,000 tonnes of Brazilian soybeans to a U.S. firm, a trader at the firm confirmed. The trader said he was not certain of the shipment date but it would probably be April or May. He could not confirm a price but said it was based on current premiums.
CORN TENDER - Taiwan's MFIG corn-buying group said on Wednesday it will tender on Thursday for one 54,000-to-56,000-tonne shipment of U.S. corn. Shipment was slated for May/June.
- South Korea is seeking 190,000 tonnes of Chinese corn for July/August shipment.
- The CCC said it would seek up to 4,620 tonnes of No. 2 or better yellow corn under its export program for Guatemala. Offers were due on March 19 and the shipment dates were slated for April 3-27.

CORN TENDER - The CCC said it was tendering on March 12 to buy up to 16,080 tonnes of U.S. yellow corn, for export to Angola. CCC said it was seeking No. 2 or better U.S. yellow corn, maximum moisture 14.5 percent, for April 1-25 shipment.

WHEAT TENDER - Tunisia on Wednesday launched a tender for the purchase of five lots of soft wheat of 25,000 tonnes each or more. Last deadline for submitting offers was set for Friday March 14 at 0930 GMT. Shipment dates for the five lots of wheat are - April 20-30, May 1-10, May 10-20, May 20-30 and June 1-10.

WHEAT TENDERS - South Korea's Daehan Flour Mills Co Ltd said on Wednesday it passed on tenders to buy 24,500 tonnes of U.S. No.1 wheat due to high offer prices. A Daehan official said it will re-invite the tenders by 2:00 p.m. (0500 GMT) on Friday.
- News was awaited on Iraq's tender for 50,000 tonnes U.S. hard red winter wheat slated for May delivery, exporters said.

- Lebanon will tender for 50,000 tonnes of U.S. hard wheat next week. Bids would be for two shipments CIF to Beirut port silos of 25,000 tonnes each, the first between April 15 and May 10 and the second between June 20 and July 15.
WHEAT TENDERS (cont.) - Sri Lanka said it would tender for 50,000 tonnes each of hard and soft wheat. The tender will close on March 13.
- The CCC is seeking up to 25,550 tonnes of wheat for donation to Jordan and Yemen for April 1-25 shipment.

- The CCC said it was tendering on March 12 to buy up to 15,180 tonnes of U.S. hard red wheat for export to Angola, April 1-25 shipment. CCC said it was seeking no. 2 or better hard red spring or hard red winter wheat.
SOYBEAN TENDER - Philippine mills on Wednesday rejected offers for 15,000 tonnes of U.S. soybeans due to high prices, traders said.

RICE TENDER - Costa Rica will seek on March 19 a total of 30,000 tonnes optional origin rough rice which would likely be from the United States or Argentina, U.S. exporters and trade sources said. One U.S. exporter said he believed the paddy rice was slated for June arrival while another said it was set for May.

MARKET TALK - The sale by Glencore Brazil of 45,000 tonnes of Brazilian soybeans to a U.S. firm appeared to make economic sense following the run-up in CBOT futures to an 8-1/2-year high Monday, some U.S. export sources said.
Sources said Brazilian soybeans could be shipped to New Orleans for around 25-1/2 cents over May CBOT futures, compared with about 24 cents for U.S. soybeans.
The higher quality of Brazilian soybeans made them effectively worth an additional 15 to 20 cents a bushel versus U.S. soybeans, one exporter said.
... The equivalent of an ocean vessel load of Canadian milling wheat is currently being railed through the United States to a Mexican client, a Canadian Wheat Board spokesman said.
... Saudi Arabia is expected to tap world markets again for feed barley and may seek to import 800,000 to 900,000 tonnes, the head of France's grain office ONIC said.
... Huge swathes of southern China's coastal areas have faced grain shortages in recent years, with the annual supply deficit totalling around 25 million tonnes, Shanghai's Business News said.

...Philippine soymeal and soybean buyers are mulling a shift from the United States, where the country buys most of its requirements, to other suppliers as U.S. supplies are currently tight, traders said on Wednesday.
